usage: wsp slate catalog [<name>]
  what a slate can hold: the index of pieces, sources, steps, functions and
  rules, or one entry in full

  --json     print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
             everything else on stderr
  --state    the state file the host serves
  --host     run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp hosts
             lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp slate write [<thread>] [<file>] [--check] [--set <path>=<json>]...
       [--press <piece>] [--row <n>] [--action <n>] [--if-version <n>]
  writes the thread's slate from a .slate file (a whole <slate> or a patch) or a
  .json document and prints its sketch; --check stores nothing, and with --set
  or --press rehearses values and a press on a copy, the file optional

  --check         validate and sketch the slate, storing nothing
  --set           with --check, a value to rehearse against, like '$i=2' or
                  'picked=1'; repeats
  --press         with --check, a piece to rehearse a press on, after the --set
                  values
  --row           the row index of the --press piece inside a list, from 0
  --action        which row action of a --press table to rehearse, from 0
  --if-version    the version a read printed; refused with V750 when the
                  document moved past it
  --json          print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
                  everything else on stderr
  --state         the state file the host serves
  --host          run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp
                  hosts lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp slate state [<thread>] [<path>=<json>...] [--start <run>]...
       [--if-version <n>]
  sets the slate's $values by path, like '$steps[2].done=true' or 'i=2', starts
  runs the person let run every time, and prints its sketch

  --if-version    the version a read printed; refused with V750 when the
                  document moved past it
  --start         a run to start now that the person said "Always in this
                  thread" to; any other answers held; repeats
  --json          print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
                  everything else on stderr
  --state         the state file the host serves
  --host          run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp
                  hosts lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp slate read [<thread>] [--values <path>]... [--no-text] [--no-sketch]
       [--document]
  the slate as it stands: the sketch, then the JSX-like form, the values,
  derived values, runs, problems and the paths named; --no-text leaves out the
  JSX-like form, --document adds the stored JSON

  --values       a path to resolve now, like '$check.exit' or
                 usage.week.percent, or * for every bound one; repeats
  --no-text      leave out the slate in the JSX-like form a patch is written
                 against
  --no-sketch    leave the sketch out
  --document     also print the stored JSON document
  --json         print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
                 everything else on stderr
  --state        the state file the host serves
  --host         run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp
                 hosts lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell
